concepts.title: Soviet System and Its Collapse
concepts.definition: The Soviet system, built after the 1917 Bolshevik revolution, concentrated economic and political power in the communist party and a centrally planned economy; by the 1980s stagnation, shortages and the arms burden with the USA had weakened it, and Gorbachev's reforms of glasnost and perestroika accelerated rather than saved the system.
concepts.key_idea: Reform exposed the rot: once censorship and central control loosened, republics and nationalities moved for independence.
concepts.textbook_ref: leps101.txt soviet system, stagnation and Gorbachev reforms sections
question_patterns: describe the features of the Soviet political-economic system

evaluate internal versus external causes of the collapse

solution_steps.explain: one-party rule and central planning defined the Soviet model from 1917
consumer shortages, technological lag and the arms race drained the economy
the failed coup and the republics' exits dissolved the union in 1991

concepts.title: Berlin Wall's Fall and Bipolarity's End
concepts.definition: The Berlin Wall, built at the height of the Cold War as its greatest symbol, was toppled by the people in 1989; two years later the Soviet Union itself dissolved, so the wall's fall and the union's end are separated by the difference of 1991 and 1989.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the wall's fall year from the Soviet end year gives the gap in years between the two events.

concepts.title: Shock Therapy and Its Consequences
concepts.definition: Post-communist states adopted shock therapy - abrupt transition to capitalism under Washington consensus prescriptions: privatisation of assets, free trade, currency convertibility; the therapy produced deep initial contraction, oligarchic capture of privatised assets and social distress, with uneven recovery across states.
concepts.key_idea: Speed was the therapy and the disease: overnight privatisation handed state assets to insiders while safety nets vanished.
concepts.textbook_ref: leps101.txt shock therapy features and consequences sections
question_patterns: define shock therapy and the Washington consensus
list the three features of shock therapy

solution_steps.explain: privatisation, free trade and convertibility arrived together and fast
output fell, inflation soared and welfare systems collapsed in the early 1990s
insider privatisation built the Russian oligarchy

concepts.title: India and Post-communist States
concepts.definition: India maintained long friendship with the Soviet Union - defence supplies, diplomatic support and trade - and after 1991 rebuilt ties with Russia and the new republics through energy, defence partnership and connectivity initiatives like the International North-South corridor.
concepts.key_idea: The end of bipolarity did not end the partnership: India and Russia re-tooled an old friendship for a multipolar market age.

solution_steps.explain: Soviet vetoes and defence supplies anchored Cold War ties

multipolarity lets India diversify while keeping old friends
